categories.any: arch=('any') — the artifact is architecture-independent, so an x86 runner may build and republish it as-is.
categories.repack: Ships a vendor-prebuilt aarch64 binary. package() only extracts and installs, never executes target code, so an x86 runner can build it with CARCH=aarch64.
categories.compile: Compiled from source, or extraction requires executing an aarch64 binary. Needs a native ARM runner.

packages.name: avd-fw
packages.note: In no repository at all -- not ALARM, not [extra], not the AUR. Without it the in-tree apple-avd driver fails to probe on every boot with 'Direct firmware load for apple/avd-fw-v2-t0.bin failed with error -2', so the video decoder sits idle. arch=('any'): the images are raw Cortex-M3 firmware, identical whatever host builds them. One build covers M1 through M4.

packages.name: cursor-bin
packages.note: Upstream omarchy-pkgs/AUR cursor-bin is arch=('x86_64') and an amd64 .deb that strips Electron. Official aarch64 edge has cursor-cli, not Cursor. Ships the vendor linux-arm64 AppImage with bundled Electron under /opt/cursor-bin so it does not collide with the Mac workaround at /opt/cursor. Icons and cursor-url-handler.desktop are unsquashed with squashfs-tools; the AppImage is not executed. pkgname stays cursor-bin. quattro-mac follow-up must delete /opt/cursor, /usr/local/bin/cursor, the two .desktop files, and hicolor icons before pacman -S, or those /usr/share paths still conflict.

packages.name: herdr
packages.note: Currently unbuildable anywhere: its PKGBUILD pins makedepends zig0.15, which Arch dropped from [extra] when it moved to zig 0.16. Only the AUR has it, as a full LLVM Zig build declaring arch=(x86_64). Left to fail visibly when it next bumps rather than carrying a zig toolchain build; fail-fast:false keeps it from blocking anything else.

packages.name: hermes-desktop

packages.name: hyprland-preview-share-picker
packages.note: Release package so omarchy-base.packages can ask for this name. Built against ALARM, not official edge Hyprland. exclude_build_deps: cargo links GTK, not the compositor; installing those runtime depends would pull ALARM hyprland. scripts/prepare-share-picker-recipe.sh rewrites RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=nightly to stable (the -git package we already shipped builds that way). After this publishes, repo-remove the leftover -git db entry and asset while no update-packages run is in progress.

packages.name: libva-v4l2_request-avd
packages.note: AVD is a stateless decoder and ffmpeg's v4l2m2m decoders are stateful, so the firmware alone gets you a /dev/video node nothing can drive. The AUR has megi's libva-v4l2_request 1.2 without the AVD fixes; this is sofus13's fork at 1.3. Installs an asahi_drv_video.so alias, which is the name libva looks for on Apple Silicon, so VA-API apps need no environment variable.

packages.name: obs-studio
packages.note: Absent from ALARM entirely, and every AUR pkgbase hardcodes obsproject's prebuilt CEF (browser dock), which exists for linux x86_64 only. The in-tree PKGBUILD builds upstream's release Sources tarball with ENABLE_BROWSER=OFF; everything else is enabled. Version bumps are edits to that PKGBUILD.

packages.name: obsidian-appimage
packages.note: split pkgbase; no build(), package() extracts the prebuilt AppImage from source_aarch64. It does so by executing that AppImage, which is fine on a native ARM runner and was the only reason this could not be built on x86.

packages.name: omarchy-nvim
packages.note: LazyVim config, arch=('any'). build() runs nvim --headless, so neovim is an extra makedepend (category any does not install runtime depends). First published artifact: the host-arch binaries to inspect are mason/packages/shfmt and stylua, not tree-sitter .so files (the official artifact has none).

packages.name: openai-codex-desktop
packages.note: not in the AUR; repacks a vendor .deb with source_aarch64. The arm64 deb bundles Node native-module prebuilds for every platform, so 8 x86 objects under */prebuilds/* are expected; the aarch64 ones sit beside them.

packages.name: pinta
packages.note: Omarchy's default simple image editor. AUR is arch=('x86_64') and hardcodes RuntimeIdentifier=linux-x64; ALARM has no pinta. ignorearch on the AUR recipe would still emit linux-x64 or fail the same way. In-tree recipe is AUR 3.1.2-1 with arch=('aarch64') and linux-arm64, depending on this repo's dotnet-*-bin packages from AUR dotnet-core-bin rather than Arch extra names that are not in ALARM. pkgname stays pinta so Restore Preinstalls does not need a rename.

Not version-tied to the release tag; it carries its own upstream version.
